source.title: An adaptive polyak heavy-ball method
source.authors: S. Saab; S. Phoha; Ming-Hui Zhu; A. Ray

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on image-classification test accuracy using a different method and measure from the version’s broader optimizer-generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper compares held-out accuracy across optimizers, but does not report whether random-label-fitting networks generalize. Its convergence experiments and cited optimizer results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out accuracy comparisons between Adam, AdamW, momentum SGD and NAG on image classifiers, directly bearing on V4 in these training settings. V4 does not require measuring a training–test gap. Results depend on the comparator; learning-rate schedules were not used, and tuning and weight decay were not matched.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct, but NAG is best on the CIFAR tasks, not all reported image tasks: AHB has the highest MNIST accuracy. The authors chiefly conclude that AHB provides convergence guarantees, strong optimization performance on several examples, and competitive image-classification performance with gamma fixed at 1.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer comparison on standard image classification rather than controlled tests of the training-test generalization gap; tuning was not matched across all optimizers.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the relative test-accuracy ordering. The authors report NAG is best on the image tasks; AHB outperforms all compared optimizers except NAG on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed AHB method achieves competitive image-classification accuracy with gamma fixed at 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An adaptive heavy-ball optimizer can achieve competitive held-out accuracy without empirical tuning of its gamma parameter.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical convergence guarantees and toy-function convergence or noise-suppression results concern optimization rather than held-out generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive heavy-ball updates can improve convergence and suppress gradient noise under the studied assumptions and examples.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say codes will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the manuscript
record.problems: The image-classification results compare test accuracy but do not report training accuracy or a train-test gap. Optimizer tuning was not matched: the paper says excessive tuning was conducted for other optimizers, while AHB used γ=1; CIFAR hyperparameters were selected on CIFAR-10 and reused on CIFAR-100. The MNIST/QMNIST table is flattened in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 8 and 9 report mean training loss and test accuracy over epochs, but provide no recoverable numeric values in the supplied text; no figure-only rows were extracted because the reported measure does not directly quantify the generalization gap. Optimizer convergence results on toy functions do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width variation beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the role of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; equal or better adaptive-method training performance; controlled broad tuning; switching to SGD; and an isolated decoupled-weight-decay recovery intervention. Training-loss curves are declared in rows_left_out but cannot be read numerically from the supplied text.
Batch-size comparisons and interventions that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied table values support the extracted assignments. Mixed comparisons must not be collapsed into one verdict. These results qualify an 'often' claim through specific exceptions; they do not establish its overall frequency. CIFAR hyperparameters were selected on CIFAR-10 and transferred to CIFAR-100; SGDm and AdamW settings came from prior work, while Adam was tuned in-house. Different regularization and omitted scheduling limit causal attribution to optimizer choice.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Language benchmarks, matched training performance, broad tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, and decoupled weight decay as a recovery intervention.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness and other measured properties tracking the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
